newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major says Labour tax rise plans revealed.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major says Labour tax rise plans revealed.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said on Thursday that a former Labour minister had "let the cat out of the bag" about tax and public spending increases under a Labour government.

"Lord Barnett, being a life peer and not threatened by the Labour leader, has clearly let the cat out of the bag about Labour's spending plans," Major told parliament at Prime Minister's question time.
"He knows their figures don't add up. He knows there is a 12 billion pounds black hole in their spending plans," Major said.
Former Labour Chief Secretary to the Treasury Lord Joel Barnett said on Wednesday he believed that if the Labour Party returned to government it would have to raise taxes.
He said he believed a Labour government would face a need to raise spending, and he hoped it would want to do so to improve health, education and other services.
"We now know the truth from the last Labour chief secretary to the Treasury," Major said.
Elections are due by May 1 and the Labour Party, up to 20 points ahead in the opinion polls, is hot favourite to take power.
Shadow Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown has pledged not to put up income tax for the life of the next government and stick to the Conservatives' spending plans for the next two years.
Barnett said he did not blame Labour leaders for their pledges to keep taxes down. "I think they were bound to do this to counter the inevitable election attack on the party," he told Reuters.
